Method, applicability and per-alternative evidence

A self-containing corridor bounds adverse gravity. Minimum supplied brake and maximum traction apply, with traction removed at its specified cut. No brake credit until both full brake and traction cut. Exact decimal-rational calculation and section selection. These sufficient conditions can be pessimistic; an unavailable bound does not prove a train cannot stop. The bound covers the mathematical model and does not approve physical inputs or the project method.

Model and interpretation limits

  • Allocation sections define failure-entry domains, not limits of train motion. Trajectories may extend beyond section boundaries and require full route coverage. Boundaries belong to both neighboring sections. Only enabled sections are allocated.
  • Envelopes are sampled maxima over applicable enabled alternatives on a common chainage/speed grid. They are not continuous guaranteed bounds.
  • A failed applicable alternative makes the corresponding envelope unavailable. Partial maxima remain separately labeled in JSON and CSV.
  • Route variants, direction and grade method are separate groups. A shared chainage datum does not prove that different route geometries are interchangeable.
  • Common-entry trajectory overlays use the specified entry chainage and commanded speed, not each vehicle’s governing start. Different profiles may add different speed allowances.
  • Mixed fleet means comparison of individual train first-arrest requirements. This version does not simulate two moving trains, fleet-pair headway, collisions or train-to-train separation.
  • Built-in vehicles and examples are synthetic. Independent project/fleet/input/numerical review is required before design use.
  • Acceleration inputs already represent the chosen load/failure condition. Mass is record-only; uniform train-length gravity is used. No force/load scaling, rotational inertia, separate track brakes/BAM, dynamic adhesion/WSP, curvature, resistance, wind, service-controller dynamics or holding/restart is modeled.
  • Nominal RK trajectories use additive position clearances. The separate continuous comparison bound covers the declared initial footprint interval through changing geometry. Step comparison remains numerical sensitivity, not a proven numerical error bound.
  • An excluded speed is outside the specified vehicle/civil entry operating domain; it is not a successful stopping calculation. Civil limits along the failure path are not supervised.
